text:
The kinexus Therapy Management Service for HHD is a cloud-based data repository and
communication system used between a healthcare facility and chronic home haemodialysis
(HHD) patients. The system securely transmits information from patients’ NxStage Cyclers via
the Nx2me App to the cloud where the data can be stored, aggregated, and presented to
healthcare providers in kinexus.
The system is not a medical device and does not control NxStage cyclers. This system shall
not be used as a substitute for direct medical intervention or emergency care. Information
collected and transmitted requires clinical judgment by an experienced medical professional.
Safety Notice
Note the following:

•
The kinexus HHD provider portal does not provide medical diagnoses or
recommendations regarding medical treatment.

•
The kinexus HHD provider portal and the content appearing on this site are not
substitutes for professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.

•
In an emergency, patients should call their local emergency assistance number.

The kinexus HHD portal is a web-based application that is typically administered by your
organisation. The one-time onboarding process includes setting up your organisation within
the kinexus HHD portal and assigning at least one admin user role that will facilitate the roll-
out of the portal to your broader home therapy staff and clinics.

For help with patient enrolment, equipment, and supplies ordering, please contact your
regional Fresenius Customer Service office.
Making clinical decisions illustration, page 9, 119x111

WARNING:
Never use the kinexus HHD Portal as the only method of making clinical decisions, monitoring,
or communicating with the patient. Risk of poor therapy outcomes.

The kinexus HHD Portal must be used in conjunction with other methods of assessing clinical
signs and symptoms to ensure proper management of patient care.

WARNING:
Changes to settings in the kinexus HHD Portal do not update settings on the cycler. The patient
or care partner must manually adjust settings on the cycler. Risk of poor therapy outcomes.

Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is a security process that requires users to provide two or
more distinct authentication factors to verify their identity before accessing the kinexus
application. MFA involves the generation of a one-time code sent via SMS to the user's mobile
number or via email address to the user's email address. The user can then use this code to
complete the login process and securely access the application.

your phone number, as shown in Figure 1-4 below.

to modify their web browser configuration. If any of these 2 conditions are not met, MFA will

text:
The kinexus HHD Remote Therapy Management Portalhelps health care providers monitor
patients on home haemodialysis. Patients use electronic rather than paper flowsheets to
transfer treatment information to the dialysis centre, as shown in Figure 2-1.

•
kinexus HHD Patient Application (Nx2me):: an iOS tablet application (on the app
store as Nx2me).

•
kinexus HHD Remote Therapy Management Portal (“portal”) : a web-based
application for health care providers.

The patient app is used at home by patients and care partners. The patient app combines
treatment information from the cycler with data entered by the patient or care partner to
create a flowsheet that is transferred to the kinexus HHD provider Portal. For more
information about patient app, refer to the kinexus HHD Patient App User Guide (Nx2me).

The Provider Portal is a web-based application that allows clinicians at the dialysis centre to
securely access patient treatment information uploaded from the Nx2me app. Prescription
settings for home haemodialysis therapy that are displayed within the Nx2me app are
configured within the kinexus HHD Provider Portal

This chapter describes the functions that are available within the kinexus HHD clinic
dashboard. The Clinic Dashboard is the landing page upon logging into the portal.

The Clinic Dashboard includes the following tabs to easily access its main functions, Figure
3-1 (A).

•
Clinic Overview, Figure 3-2 (A), provides an overview of All patients associated with
the clinic and displays the number of patients that currently have Therapy Gaps. And
the number of patients in their First 90 Days, calculated from the date of their first
treatment recorded in the kinexus HHD system.

•
Alerts & Alarms – Last 7 Days, Figure 3-2 (B), displays the patients list along with
treatments within the last 7 days that have received Clinical Alerts, Cycler Alarms
and/or Cycler Cautions.
•

•
All Treatments, Figure 3-2 (C), this table lists flowsheets that the clinic has received
for the patients within the clinic for the last 7 days treatments.

text:
The Clinic Overview Card displays All Patients, Therapy Gaps and First 90 days with a
count of the total number of clinic patients associated with each classification. The All Patients
count includes all clinic patients that are enrolled in kinexus HHD. The Therapy Gap count
includes all patients that have not sent a treatment within the last 3 days or more. First 90
Days count includes all clinic patients calculated from the date of their first treatment recorded
in the kinexus HHD system.

Clicking All Figure 3-3 (A), takes you to the Patients section which displays a list of all active
patients in the selected clinic as shown in Figure 3-4. Patients are sorted alphabetically by last
name and include details such as HHD status, ID, Sex, date of birth (DOB), Therapy Gap,
HHD Start date, 1st treatment date, and the number of unreviewed treatments.

Clicking Therapy Gaps Figure 3-3 (B), takes you to the Patients list, displaying patients who
have not recorded a treatment in the past three days or more. For more information, see the
Patients section.

Clicking First 90 Days Figure 3-3 (B), takes you to the Patients list, displaying only those
patients whose first treatment has been recorded within the last 90 days in the kinexus HHD
system. For more information, see the Patients section.

The Clinical Alerts & Alarms card displays treatments that received a clinical alert and/or
cycler alarm and cautions within the last 7 days. Each row contains the patient's name,
DOB, the number of treatments impacted, the count of clinical alerts, the total count of cycler
alarms and cautions. For more information, see the Alert Criteria section in Chapter 4:
Patient Profile.

Clicking the arrow adjacent to the patient's name, Figure 3-5 (A), displays list of treatment
dates with the total treatment duration and number of clinical alerts and/or cycler alarms and
cautions, as shown in Figure 3-6 (A).

The Last 7 Days Treatments table lists all treatments recorded in the past seven days for
patients associated with the clinic, as shown in Figure 3-7. Treatments are listed
chronologically by the newest date. To sort treatments from oldest to newest dates, click the
downward arrow next to the Date, Start column header, Figure 3-7 (A).

Search by patient
The search bar at the left side of this screen enables users to search for patients by first
name or last name. Searching happens automatically once you enter the first letter into the
search bar, Figure 3-7 (B). To return to the full patient list, remove your search parameters
from the search bar.

The following information is displayed in the Last 7 Days Treatments table, Figure 3-7 (C):

•
Date, Start displays the date when the treatment started in DD/MM/YY format. A blue
dot beside the date means the treatment has not yet been reviewed. Clicking on the
treatment date will take you to that patient’s treatment flowsheet page. For more
information, see Chapter 5: Treatment Flowsheet.

•
Patient Name displays the patient's name (last name, first name) and date of birth.
Clicking on the patient’s name will take you to that patient profile page. For more
information, see Chapter 4: Patient Profile.

•
Alarms indicators appear when a treatment value falls outside a prescribed range
as defined by the alert criteria.

The number adjacent to the alert icon indicates the total count of clinical alerts.

This chapter provides detailed information about the data available within the kinexus HHD
patient profile, including:

•
All treatment data
•
Prescription details
•
Alert criteria
•
Lifestyle goals
•
Flowsheet calendar report
•
Trending alarm & caution data

Clicking on any of the patient’s names, will display the respective patient's profile screen.
Here, you can view the patient's demographic details, including date of birth (DOB), Sex,
unique identifiers (such as NHS number), and HHD Start Date.

The Patient Profile screen includes the following tabs to easily access its main functions.

The Flowsheet Calendar displays the percentage of prescribed dialysate that was processed
during the treatment (percentage = dialysate processed / dialysate prescribed). The calendar
will display this information for all treatments received during the last six calendar weeks,
including both confirmed and unconfirmed flowsheets.

If the patient performed two treatments on the same day, two graphics will appear for that day.
If the patient performed more than two treatments in the same day, the + icon, Figure 4-2 (A),
appears, in this scenario please refer to the Treatment Table to view information for all
treatments.

Hovering your mouse over the graphics will display the treatment date, time, and the
percentage of dialysate completed.

Clicking on graphics will take you to the Treatment Flowsheet screen. For more information,
see Chapter 5: Treatment Flowsheet.

Clicking on download icon, Figure 4-2 (B), allows you to download and save the Flowsheet
Calendar as a PDF, which can then be printed on a local printer.

Any alarms or cautions that occur on the NxStage cycler during dialysis are recorded in the
treatment flowsheet. The Total Alarms & Cautions card provides a cross-treatment view,
showing the total number of alarms and cautions across all treatments.The graph displays the
number of alarms and/or cautions that occurred during the last 20 treatments. If the number
of alarms and/or cautions exceeds ten, they are represented as "10+."

The alert criteria entered and displayed in the patient profile determines the ranges at which
a clinical alert (
) will be displayed.

While in the patient profile, the alert criteria card displays a preview of alert criteria thresholds
that have been configured for blood pressure and temperature.

Clicking the
icon, Figure 4-1 (D), takes you to the Alert Criteria section under the Therapy
Management tab, where you can view and edit the patient’s blood pressure, temperature, and
other alerts. For more information, see the Therapy Management section.

The Lifestyle goals card displays lifestyle goals for patients and/or care-partners as entered
by clinicians into kinexus HHD. The date of the most recent update is displayed.

Once the patient and care partner details are entered, click the Save button, Figure 4-4 (A),
to successfully save the information. Clicking Cancel, Figure 4-4 (B) or the X, Figure 4-4 (C),
will take you back to the Patient Profile screen without making any changes to the lifestyle
goals.

The Treatments tab, Figure 4-5, lists treatments according to start date and time. Only
treatments that your user role and designated clinic authorize you to view will be visible. To
sort treatments from oldest to newest dates, click the downward arrow next to the Date, Start
column header For more details on the data displayed, see section, Last 7 Days Treatments.

At the top of the Treatments list is a sort drop-down menu, Figure 4-5 (A), which allows you to
sort the list in four ways, as shown in Figure 4-6.

•
All, Figure 4-6 (A), displays a complete list of treatments received for that patient.

•
Last 7 Days, Figure 4-6 (B), displays treatments received within the last seven days.

•
Un-Reviewed, Figure 4-6 (C), displays treatments that have not yet been reviewed.

•
Un-Submitted, Figure 4-6 (D), displays treatments of that patient that have not yet
been submitted and remain editable.

The treatment table, Figure 4-5 (B), displays a list of information related to each treatment.
For more information on the treatment table, see the Last 7 Days Treatments Table section.

Clicking the checkbox next to a specific treatment date, enables the Mark as Reviewed or
Mark as Un-Reviewed, Figure 4-5 (C), buttons, at the top of the table. For more information.
See How to Review Treatments section.

Clicking on treatment will take you to the Treatment Flowsheet screen. For more information,
see Chapter 5: Treatment Flowsheet.

text:
The Prescription Summary screen displays the status of the therapy in the top left corner. This
feature provides clinicians with essential information regarding patient engagement, aiding in
treatment monitoring and management.

•
Initially, when clinicians add or modify the therapy, the status appears as Not
acknowledged by patient, as shown in Figure 4-9 (A).

•
Once the patient has viewed and acknowledged the therapy change in the Nx2me
App, the status changes to Acknowledged by patient along with the date, as shown
in Figure 4-10 (A).

The Alert Criteria entered and displayed in the patient profile determines the ranges at which
a clinical alert (
) will be displayed.

The Alert Criteria section provides an overview of the patient's alert criteria thresholds that
have been configured for blood pressure and temperature.

Here clinicians can enter or edit the blood pressure, temperature, and other alerts for that
individual patient. After making the necessary changes, click the Save button, Figure 4-11 (A),
to save the updated therapy details successfully. To discard edits and restore the original
values, click Clear, Figure 4-11 (B).

•
Dialysate Vol. Deviation: The volume of dialysate used in a treatment deviate from
the prescribed volume by more than the specified amount in litres (L).

•
Dry Weight Deviation: The patient’s dry weight at the end of a treatment deviates
from the prescribed dry weight by more than the specified amount in kilogrammes (kg).

•
No. of Cycler Alarms: The total number of cycler alarms is greater than or equal to
the specified value.

A treatment flowsheet is an electronic record sent from the patient app (Nx2me) to the Provider
Portal that provides details about each dialysis treatment. Each flowsheet is a combination of
data collected directly from the cycler and data entered by the patient into the Nx2me app.

The Flowsheet screen displays the status of the treatment flowsheet in the top left corner of
the screen.

•
Once the patient confirms the treatment in the Nx2me app, the status appears as
Submitted by patient along with the date and timestamp, as shown in Figure 5-2
(A).
•
If the patient has not confirmed the treatment  that status will be displayed as Un-
Submitted, as shown in Figure 5-3 (A).

o
When flowsheets are in an un-submitted state they are still editable by the
patient
o
Flowsheets that have a dialysate volume processed and treatment duration
associated with them will automatically be submitted after 3 days.
Flowsheets that have been automatically submitted will display Submitted by
System along with the date and timestamp.

The Dialysate section displays the amount of dialysate fluid processed during the treatment
and the amount prescribed by the patient's physician in litres (L), as shown in Figure 5-5. It
includes the following measurements:

•
Processed, L: The cycler dialysate volume processed during the treatment, in
litres (L).

•
Prescribed, L: The volume of dialysis prescribed to use for each treatment, in
litres (L).

The Ultrafiltration section displays the target and actual litres (L) of ultrafiltration removed
from the patient during treatment as well as the average ultrafiltration rate in litres per hour
(L/hr), as shown in Figure 5-6. It includes the following measurements:

•
Target, L: The prescribed ultrafiltration volume to be removed during the
treatment, in litres (L).

•
Actual, L: The ultrafiltration volume removal achieved during the treatment in
litres (L).

The Alerts, Alarms, and Cautions card displays clinical alerts, cycler alarms, and cycler
cautions recorded for an individual treatment. as shown in Figure 5-8. It includes the following
measurements:

•
Pre Temperature, °C – Patient’s body temperature before starting the treatment, in
Celsius (°C).

•
Post Temperature, °C - Patient’s body temperature after completing the treatment,
in Celsius (°C).

•
Post-Dialysis Weight, kg - Patient’s weight after completing the treatment, in
kilograms (kg).

•
Number of cycler alarms exceeded Alert Criteria threshold – The total number of
cycler alarms that exceeded the alert criteria threshold.

•
Dialysate Processed, L – Displays the cycler dialysate volume processed during the
treatment, in litres (L).

•
During treatment – BP, mmHg - Patient’s blood pressure recorded during the

The Weight section displays weight data entered by the patient before and after treatment,
as well as the weights used to calculate treatment targets, as shown in Figure 5-9.

•
Pre-Dialysis Weight, kg: The weight of the patient before starting the treatment, in
kilogrammes (kg).
•
Weight to Remove, kg: The calculated amount of weight to be removed from the
patient during treatment in kilogrammes (kg).
•
Post-Dialysis Weight, kg: The weight of the patient after completing the treatment, in
kilogrammes (kg).
•
Dry Weight (Rx), kg: The patient's prescribed target weight post-dialysis, in
kilogrammes (kg).
•
Prev. Post-Weight, kg: The patient's previous post-dialysis weight. If available from
previous flowsheets, this value is captured by the Nx2me app and added to the
flowsheet automatically; otherwise, it is entered by the patient, in kilogrammes (kg).

•
Dialysate Flow Rate, L/hr: The rate of dialysate fluid flow in litres per hour (L/hr).

•
Initial Blood Flow Rate, ml/min: The initial (starting) rate of blood flow in millilitres per
minute (ml/min).
•
Target Blood Flow Rate, ml/min: The target rate of blood flow in millilitres per minute

(ml/min).

The Patient Notes & Photos section displays notes or images entered by the patient for this

User management tasks can be performed by users with an admin role. Within the user
management section, Admin users may create new users, assign user roles, or view and
edit existing user roles and information.

Once the Menu icon, Figure 6-1 (A), is clicked from the side navigation bar, the screen-
overlay menu appears, as shown in Figure 6-2. Clicking Users button, Figure 6-2 (A), takes
the user to the User Management page where a list of users is displayed. Clicking kinexus
HHD button, Figure 6-2 (B), will take user back to the kinexus HHD portal.

The search bar Figure 6-3 (B). on top of user list allows you to search for users by first, last

name, or email address. Searching happens automatically once you enter the letters in

the search bar. To return to the full user list, remove your search parameters from the search

bar.

Clicking Create User from the user list screen, Figure 6-3 (C), will open a create user screen,
Figure 6-4. Here, you can enter the new user details, such as First name, Last name, Email
Address, Phone Prefix (i.e., Country Code) with Phone Number, Language and select the
preferred clinic from the drop-down list. Additionally, you can assign the necessary roles to
the user under the Roles. Kinexus Home HD User role must be selected for each user to
access the kinexus HHD application.

o
Can create HHD user and assign the roles and clinics to the user.
o
Can read/modify data from HHD UI.
o

service support required).

•
Kinexus Home HD User
o
Can read/modify data from HHD UI.
o

o

For any user, clicking on the ellipsis ( ) symbol adjacent to their name in the user table list
opens a screen-overlay menu, as shown in Figure 6-6. Clicking on Edit, Figure 6-6 (A), takes
you to the edit user screen (Figure 6-7).
